title: Covered calls have negative asymmetry: four ways to reduce it
summary: Covered calls take the elevator down and the escalator up: full downside, capped upside. The speaker gives fixes: choose strikes on purpose (OTM for more upside, ITM for more downside protection), sell fewer calls than shares you own, such as 4 contracts on 500 shares, and keep some names with no calls as the growth part of the portfolio.

steps.caption: Sell only 4 calls, one strike further out, instead of 5.
At expiry: a normal covered call below the strike, and still rising above it.
Above the strike the uncovered 100 shares keep participating in the upside.
Premium lowers breakeven a little. An ITM strike would protect more on the downside.
The downside is still almost the full stock loss: the elevator down.

takeaways: Covered calls keep the downside and cap the upside.
Pick OTM strikes for upside or ITM strikes for downside protection.
Sell fewer calls than shares, and leave some names uncovered for growth.
caveats: Part of the transcript is cut, so one of the four ideas is missing.
Covered calls hold stock; check the owner's options-only rule before deploying.

backtest.note: Monthly 25-delta covered call on liquid names; OTM strike to keep more upside.
